title: The Division of Living Water
english: To know and not to know means that one must grasp one thing or another, rather than the knowing and not-knowing signifying something else.

Zach. 14:8–9: And in that day living water shall come out from Jerusalem, half of it to the first sea and half of it to the last sea, and it shall be thus in summer and in winter. And the Lord shall be king over all the earth. On the known day of the Lord, living water shall come out from Jerusalem, 'of the heavenly city of the living God,' of which the half shall be toward the first sea, the rest half toward the last sea, going, the same thing happening not only in summer but also in spring, over all the earth, that is, of the humans, the Lord reigning.

Since nothing sensible or historical is being manifested by the prophecy, all of it must be received by anagogical lifting up. For the living water coming out from the intelligible Jerusalem, which sees the peace of the Church, is the spiritual law, or rather the knowledge of ecclesiastical understandings, which, going out toward the sea, makes it sweet and makes it calm, being driven out against every winter and overturning it.

This indeed the vision has attained clarity, as we were explaining recently the one in Isaiah having it thus: 'The whole earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea' (Isa 11:9). For just as the divine love, that which is from God toward those experiencing good, and that of the benefactors toward the magnanimous, 'covers a multitude of sins' (1 Pet 4:8), vanishing [the sins], but not guarding [them], and covering what was done crudely, so the knowledge of God, existing as living water, covers the seas, changing them into sweetness and something drinkable.
Thus the living water coming out from Jerusalem into the first and last sea, having lifted up every dizziness and storm, every saltiness and bitterness, prosperity and calm...

He will prepare a spring and a fountain so that seas shall no longer be. Living water having been divided, it came upon them; for one half of it went into the first, and the other half went into the last, which has received it, not in the summer alone but also in the springtime.

And of such a benefit existing, the Lord will rule over all the earth, according to the things said in the Psalms, where it says: 'The Lord has reigned, let the earth rejoice' (Ps 96:1), and where it says: 'Say among the nations: The Lord has reigned, and indeed he has established the inhabited world, which shall not be shaken' (Ps 97:1). Then the inhabited world is established so as to remain unshakeable, when the first sea, being the assembly of the Jews, has been made sweet, and the last, being the calling of the Gentiles. Both these seas were being filled with disturbance and storm before the reception of the gospel and the faith into the Savior, and rather into the Holy Trinity.

Try if it is possible to divide the living water into the two covenants, the new and the old, this happening when the water has become outside of Jerusalem. And from it there went out a little while 'into the whole earth' arrived 'the sound' of the words of God and 'his words to the ends of the inhabited world', as everywhere a 'sweet fragrance' is being spiritually 'offered to God and a pure sacrifice', since the Lord has been greatly revealed among all the nations.

The living water having been divided into a half and a half into the two covenants, it was within in Jerusalem, being guarded under the shadow of the law and of the antiquity of the letter, rather being covered, while the peak of winter was holding; but when the spring was received, the things having blossomed upon the earth and the voice of the vintage calling in the land, according to that which was said in the Song of Songs, 'the fig tree has yielded its figs, the vines are fragrant, the winter has passed, the rain has gone, it has departed, the flowers appeared in the land' (Song 2:11-12).
